title: Modi Urges Putin to End Ukraine War in Direct Bishkek Appeal
excerpt: Indian PM tells Russian president that 'every day spent in war sets humanity back,' calls for moving from 'endless war to end of war' at SCO Summit.
body:
• PM Modi told Putin that India supports all peace efforts in Ukraine and will continue to do so, urging a move "from endless war to end of war"
  • The Bishkek meeting was the first Modi-Putin bilateral of 2026, held on the sidelines of the 26th SCO Summit in Kyrgyzstan
  • Modi raised the safety of Indian seafarers affected by Black Sea maritime disruptions and invited Putin to the BRICS Summit in India on September 12-13
  • Putin responded that Russia is "moving in this direction" but the Kremlin has repeatedly said it will end the war only on its own terms

Prime Minister Narendra Modi delivered a pointed appeal to Russian President Vladimir Putin on Monday to end the war in Ukraine, telling him at the start of their bilateral talks in Bishkek that continued conflict comes at a direct cost to humanity.

"Every day that the war continues, humanity is, in effect, set back a step, whilst every step towards peace gives all of humanity real hope for peace," Modi said, according to a Kremlin transcript of their exchange on the sidelines of the 26th Shanghai Cooperation Organisation summit. "We need to move from endless war to an end to the war, to a cessation of hostilities."

"The land of Gandhi and the land of Buddha share a single message: the path of peace."

— Narendra Modi, at the SCO Summit in Bishkek

A Direct Message, Delivered Publicly

Modi called Putin "my friend" and hailed growing economic ties between the two countries before switching from Hindi to English to deliver the core message on Ukraine. He told Putin that India supports "all and every effort" for peace and would continue to do so, framing the appeal as both a diplomatic position and a moral imperative rooted in India's civilisational heritage.

Putin responded briefly: "Thank you very much, Prime Minister. We are moving forward along this path," according to Russian state media. The Kremlin later said Putin briefed Modi on the progress of what Russia calls its "special military operation" in Ukraine, the state TASS news agency reported.

The exchange underscored the limits of India's influence. Russia has repeatedly said it will end the war only on its own terms — conditions Ukraine has dismissed as demands to capitulate. The war, now in its fifth year, has killed tens of thousands and displaced millions.

Seafarer Safety and Maritime Trade

Beyond Ukraine, the two leaders discussed the impact of conflicts in West Asia and the Black Sea region on maritime trade routes and the safety of Indian seafarers. According to the Ministry of External Affairs, Modi raised the issue directly with Putin, underlining the human and economic cost of the conflict for Indian nationals working on commercial vessels in affected waters.

The leaders reviewed bilateral cooperation across defence, energy, space, and people-to-people ties, and welcomed the outcome of the 27th India-Russia Inter-Governmental Commission on Trade, held on August 24 in Moscow.

BRICS Invitation and Strategic Ties

Modi extended a formal invitation to Putin to attend the 18th BRICS Summit in India, scheduled for September 12-13. India holds the BRICS chairship for 2026. The two leaders agreed to deepen their Special and Privileged Strategic Partnership, which the MEA described as having "shown resilience in the backdrop of geopolitical uncertainties."

India, along with China, remains one of the largest buyers of Russian oil, a trade that has helped Moscow replenish its wartime budget after sweeping Western sanctions. That energy relationship forms the economic backdrop against which Modi's peace message is delivered — and received.

What's Next

The Bishkek meeting was the first bilateral between the two leaders this year, following Putin's two-day state visit to India in December 2025 for the 23rd India-Russia Annual Summit. In a visible display of personal rapport, Modi and Putin travelled together in the same car to the opening ceremony of the World Nomad Games at Bishkek Arena after their talks concluded.

India's diplomatic balancing act — maintaining strategic ties with Moscow while pressing for a negotiated end to the Ukraine conflict — faces its next test at the September BRICS Summit. Whether Modi's public appeals translate into meaningful movement toward peace remains uncertain, but the directness of Monday's message marked a notable escalation in India's rhetorical push for an end to hostilities.
